title: The Plan Refill Date and Early-Claim Override Codes — Prescription Insurance on File Claims Reference
content:
## Rule

Under **Prescription Insurance on File**, the plan pays a routine claim for a prescription no earlier than the date of service of the previous paid claim for this prescription plus the plan refill days.

- **Plan refill days** are the previous paid claim's days supply multiplied by the class's plan early refill threshold percent and divided by 100, with any fraction of a day dropped.
- The previous date of service is day 0 and calendar days are counted; a claim dated on the plan refill date itself is paid.

An earlier claim is rejected refill too soon unless it carries a submission clarification code the class accepts on an early claim and the override count allows it:

| Code on the early claim | Paid when |
|---|---|
| Vacation supply | the prescription's paid, unreversed vacation-supply claims in the current plan year are below the class's vacation-supply overrides per plan year |
| Lost or stolen | the prescription's paid, unreversed lost-or-stolen claims in the current plan year are below the class's lost-or-stolen overrides per plan year |
| Therapy change | the class pays a therapy-change override |

## Kestrel's own date

The plan's date and Kestrel's own refill-eligible date under Prescriptions both apply, and the later of the two governs a routine refill. A plan override never lets Kestrel dispense before its own date unless Prescriptions also allows that early-fill reason.

## Worked plan refill dates (hypothetical: previous paid claim of 30 days on 1 April)

| Class threshold | 30 days multiplied by the threshold, divided by 100 | Plan refill days (fraction dropped) | Earliest routine claim date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 75 percent | 22.5 | 22 | 23 April |
| 80 percent | 24 | 24 | 25 April |
| 85 percent | 25.5 | 25 | 26 April |

At an 80 percent threshold, a routine claim on 24 April is rejected refill too soon and one on 25 April is paid.

## Override count (hypothetical)

A class allows 1 lost-or-stolen override per plan year. The prescription already has one paid lost-or-stolen claim this plan year that was not reversed: the count is not below 1, so an early claim with the lost or stolen code is rejected refill too soon. Had that earlier claim been reversed, the count would be 0 and the override would be paid.
